body:
I don't have a strong opinion on this, but I'd consider reducing this down to a max of 8 players. The benefit of doing so is that (1) the API surface/number of constants is smaller and (2) we reduce the number of focused elements that need to be tracked by 4x, which may end up being a performance improvement.

I admit that these aren't the most compelling reasons, but it may be better to start smaller, since we can always add more players.

body:
What's the purpose for this class? Is it for one of these two points from the proposal?:

> 2. `ProjectSettings` will get new settings which define the mapping from `(device type,device index)` to a "player" layer. These values will determine which "player" layer an `InputEvent` gets assigned to.

> 3. `InputMap` actions will now implicitly be defined for each "player" layer. This means that developers do not need to configure actions ahead of time or manually duplicate actions; no changes to the `InputMap` UI are required. 

If so, I don't think we'll end up needing a custom editor UI. If I understand the intent here correctly, I think the mapping can just be defined in some new [project settings](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_projectsettings.html). As far as how those settings would be defined, I don't have a concrete proposal yet, but it should be doable.
Do we need to restrict mouse actions to player `1`? Is it possible to look up the current player "owning" mouse input?

body:
Yeah this is probably the part I'm struggling more with.
You are correct that we may not need a new UI to map devices and players, I think I just misunderstood your proposal.
The issue that comes to my mind is "Does it make sense to map devices and players ahead of time in some settings, when devices can connect amd disconnect at any time? Also, keyboard, mouse and the first connected controller are always (?) defined by a device with index 0".
We probably need to clarify better how this should work, and also have some new API for the developers to control this mapping stuff at runtime...
Can we do something about subdividing the kb, mouse, controller 1 having all index 0?
Another issue, I guess, is that now through `InputMap` you can have for the same action multiple inputs from different devices. But when you scale it to multiple players, it's not like the other players will have their own keyboards. So there's this default situation where player 0 has its `InputMap` with both keyboard and controller, then the other players only have the controller inputs. Should we clarify (and how) that if you assign to an action in `InputMap` both keyboard and controller inputs, the keyboard will only work for the first player? And what if I wanted to give the keyboard to player 2 , and controller to player 1?
Let me know what you think, since we should try to keep this as simple as possible, but mapping seems pretty complex to manage.

Yes, we can reduce the number of players.
What about having 16? Since Godot already supports up to 16 joypads.
For now I'll reduce it to 8 as you said, because if I remember correctly most of the times PCs can't even go past 4 with XInput, so it does make sense.

I was also thinking we may manage this with some macros and let the developer choose how many player layers he wants (8 by default for official builds, or even 4). It could work the same way as when you compile with double precision, using some flag. I can already see how some devs may want to make a game with more than 8 players, and we shouldn't constrain them to change the core manually if we have the occasion to make it modular.
DirectInput + XInput limits you to 8 gamepads in practice, and I've never heard of a game supporting more than 8 local players anyway.

body: Please correct me if I'm wrong, but I think we need to have one `ActionState` _per player_ instead of storing a `PlayerId` property on the `ActionState`. Otherwise, if two players simultaneously activate an action, won't `Input::is_action_pressed` (and related methods) only be able to detect that one of those players is pressing the action?

Even though, it isn't event probably complete.
I was thinking to make it like this:
```cpp
// Represents which player is pressing/releasing the action.
BitField<PlayerMask> active_players = PLAYER_1;
```
But I'm realizing that this data would not represent the fact that e.g. one player is pressing it, the other is releasing just now etc. Because it is only referencing the current state of one action, when in reality we want to manage a multitude of them, because each one should have its different state (or am I misunderstanding something?).
So, it's more something like:
```cpp
HashMap<StringName, ActionState[MAX_PLAYERS]> action_states;
```
Or make sure that we do some kind of mapping for `DeviceState`, since it's is already taking care of the multiple devices (and hence players?).
```cpp
HashMap<int, DeviceState> device_states;
// Map this in some way?
```
What do you think? @coffeebeats 
EDIT: I'm really not sure, it is confusing. Maybe it's just a matter of changing the type from `PlayerId` to `PlayerMask`. Do you have some test in mind to check if the behaviour is correct or not?

Hello @groud, sorry to bother you.
As you can see in the thread there is some confusion about how to address the new implementation of multiplayer, here especially about how you could correctly register pressing/releasing actions with multiple players. I'm pinging you since I saw it was your commit to [rework](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/8cfcd3625359befb28f7d239cd4a7821ab45c338#diff-4b130ca00df1a3ab5088ddab3696b80c8f25456c1ad2eba5b07db14facff1993) `ActionState`, so I hope you can give us some more context, because I find it pretty confusing and can't understand it.

My first question is: giving that `pressed_*_frame` represents the frame at which the `ActionState` is pressed/released, how does the system know this information in case of multiple devices?
I see there is a `DeviceState` struct that someway accounts for different devices, but only for `pressed`, `strength` and `raw_strength`, so I assume there is no way to see if device 1 just pressed the action, if for example device 0 pressed the same action in the past and is still keeping it pressed, right? Sorry if it's confusing.

I'm guessing that considering the direction of this PR, that is based on implementing a `player` layer each device maps to, the design of `ActionState` needs to be changed accordingly, and probably for the better.
Or am I failing to see something and it's just an easy tweak?

What's the best direction to take here?
1. Have a `action_states` `HashMap` for each player, making it an array of 8 elements `HashMap<StringName, ActionState> action_states[PLAYERS_MAX];`;
2. Have the value of the `HashMap` for `action_states` be an array of 8 elements `HashMap<StringName, ActionState[]> action_states;`
3. Implementing some sort of mapping inside `ActionState`, for example linking the device id of `device_states` to a player.
Sorry if I used C++ syntax, it was just to explain the ideas.

body:
Hi. No problem!

> My first question is: giving that pressed_*_frame represents the frame at which the ActionState is pressed/released, how does the system know this information in case of multiple devices?

In the action state, you have the `HashMap<int, DeviceState> device_states;`.  This this tracks the state per device ID. IIRC the device ID is always 0 for keyboard and mouse , and 1, 2, 3, etc. for gamepads. Then, within the DeviceState struct you get this:
```
struct DeviceState {
	bool pressed[MAX_EVENT] = { false };
	float strength[MAX_EVENT] = { 0.0 };
	float raw_strength[MAX_EVENT] = { 0.0 };
};
```
It tracks each state per event in the action map. So like, if multiple buttons of the same gamepad are bound the the same action, each button needs to be tracked separately. That's what the array is for.

>  I see there is a DeviceState struct that someway accounts for different devices, but only for pressed, strength and raw_strength, so I assume there is no way to see if device 1 just pressed the action, if for example device 0 pressed the same action in the past and is still keeping it pressed, right? Sorry if it's confusing.

Exactly. If you press two buttons (on multiple devices or not) mapped to the same action, only one "just pressed" event will trigger. That's on purpose and it should be kept that way, as otherwise it could lead to inconsistencies where the state is not consistent. (like, for example, if you release one key after the other and have two "just released" event, then the first event would trigger but the state would still be "pressed", as the other key is not released yet. Hope that's clear)

> I'm guessing that considering the direction of this PR, that is based on implementing a player layer each device maps to, the design of ActionState needs to be changed accordingly, and probably for the better.
Or am I failing to see something and it's just an easy tweak?

Well, I am not sure. I guess it depends on how you see it. Either you consider an action as common to all players, then keep action state per player, or you consider actions as being assigned to each player with some sort of an additional per-player index. It kind of depends on how you map events to actions.

> What's the best direction to take here?

I think 3 is likely the best approach I'd say. But the problem is that, in the end, you have to assign a device to each local player, which means assigning different events independently. But I am not even sure that is enough, some games do allow you to play with two players on the same device (like either left side of the keyboard + right side of the keyboard, or even a single gamepad, like in Overcooked)

In general I kind of feel we might need some sort of indirection for that anyway. The current state of the input mapping API was built to require being very specific about the event associated to an action, and the general approach was to have a list of actions a bit like this:
```
action_jump_0 (-> for player 0)
    - event: A pressed on gamepad 0
action_attack_0
    - event: B pressed on gamepad 0
action_jump_1 (-> for player 1)
    - event: A pressed on gamepad 1
action_attack_1
    - event: A pressed on gamepad 1
```
I don't really think there's a simple way to change that easily. It likely requires some sort of indirection, with "control profiles", that could get assigned to a specific device (or not), and remapped dynamically with an API.
But that requires significant UI work, so not sure how's the best way to solve it.

Should we perhaps have default values here to keep compatibility?

I went to try the PR with a project I have using Terrain3D and it gave me errors on some spots of the plugin that use gui_get_focus_owner, I imagine if it had a default value there with the first player ID or all player IDs it would solve those kinds of compatibility issues:

```
 ERROR: res://addons/terrain_3d/src/tool_settings.gd:203 - Parse Error: Too few arguments for "gui_get_focus_owner()" call. Expected at least 1 but received 0.
  ERROR: res://addons/terrain_3d/src/tool_settings.gd:203 - Parse Error: Too few arguments for "gui_get_focus_owner()" call. Expected at least 1 but received 0.

```
I'm fixing this right now. Thank you!
